interview.hardest_part: Sustained real-time combat across multiple floors. Each turn I see one static screenshot and choose one discrete action while the game continues running, so I cannot dodge enemy projectiles the way a human player would. Boss fights demand simultaneous movement and aimed shooting that is very hard to coordinate one input at a time.
interview.likely_failure: Accumulating too much chip damage in regular rooms and arriving at a boss fight with one or two hearts remaining, then dying to a pattern I could not react to in time. Floor 3 bosses like Chub or Fistula have wide hitboxes and spread attacks that are especially punishing under screenshot-based play. Health lost cannot be recovered easily without luck on drop RNG.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Items and pickups are collected by walking over them, which requires no timing. Room doors stay closed until every enemy dies, giving me a clear binary completion state I can read from the screenshot rather than estimating. The minimap marks room types, so I can plan a path to the treasure room and boss room efficiently rather than wandering. Bombs and active items are deliberate one-shot inputs I can reason about without reaction time.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Enemy projectiles move in real time while I am deciding, so the game state when my input lands will differ from what the screenshot showed. I cannot hold a direction key to strafe continuously — each step is a single action — making sustained dodge patterns nearly impossible. Starting with zero items and three red hearts leaves almost no margin for early errors. If the run ends, there is only one attempt, so a single bad boss fight on floor 1 resets all progress.
